content.title: About
content.content: Poppy seed dressing is a thick sauce made from ground poppy seeds, vegetable oil, vinegar, and spices. It has a delicate nutty aroma, a mildly sweet flavor, and a characteristic creamy texture. It is used in salads, as a marinade for fish and meat, and as a sauce for vegetable dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Poppy seeds are rich in linoleic acid, which gives the dressing its distinctive scent.
Traditional recipes come from Eastern European cuisines, especially Polish and Russian kitchens.
Apple cider vinegar is often used in the original recipe to highlight the natural sweetness of poppy seeds.
The dressing can be kept in the refrigerator for up to two weeks without losing flavor or texture.
Ground poppy seeds help stabilize the emulsion, preventing separation.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Poppy seed oil contains polyunsaturated fatty acids that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of calcium and magnesium
items.content: Poppy seeds provide minerals that contribute to bone strength and normal muscle function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Vitamin E and flavonoids in the dressing help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from poppy seeds aids regular bowel movements.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: The dressing’s sweetness comes from the natural flavor of poppy seeds, without large amounts of added sugar.

items.title: Poppy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to poppy seeds.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because of the oil, the dressing is relatively calorie‑dense and should be used in moderation.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Poppy seeds contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Drizzle the dressing over salads, add it to marinades for fish, chicken or pork, use as a sauce for roasted vegetables, or serve as a dip with bread and crackers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dressing in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C. Stir before each use if separation occurs. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or changes color.
